These supplementary academic regulations define a fictional set of university rules covering academic registration, course selection, credits, semester progression, examinations, attendance, leave, academic records, and administrative procedures. Where another document contains a more specific provision, the applicable provisions should be considered together before determining which rule applies.

The academic year is divided into an odd semester and an even semester. The odd semester normally begins in July and concludes after the end-semester assessment period. The even semester normally begins in January and concludes after the corresponding end-semester assessment period. Exact teaching dates may be published separately by the academic office.

Students are responsible for checking the academic calendar, course registration notices, examination notices, and other official communicatio

academic calendar, course registration notices, examination notices, and other official communications made available through the university's designated student portal. A student cannot claim that a deadline did not apply merely because the student did not personally read a notice that had been properly published through the designated channel.

A student must complete semester registration within the period announced by the academic office. Registration normally requires confirmation of the student's programme, semester, selected courses, and any outstanding administrative requirements. A registration request may be held for review where required documents or payments are incomplete.

Students should verify their registered courses after registration closes. Errors in course registration should be reported promptly. A course appearing

registration closes. Errors in course registration should be reported promptly. A course appearing on a student's timetable does not, by itself, establish that the course has been successfully registered if the student's official academic record does not contain the course.

Each programme has an approved curriculum specifying compulsory courses, elective courses, practical components, projects, and other academic requirements. Students may not replace a compulsory course with an unrelated elective merely because the replacement carries the same number of credits.

Where an elective has a stated prerequisite, the prerequisite must normally be satisfied before registration. A department may permit an exception when an approved academic process explicitly authorises i

tion. A department may permit an exception when an approved academic process explicitly authorises it. Such an exception should be recorded in the student's academic record.

A student may not normally register for two courses whose scheduled final examinations occur at the same time. If a timetable conflict is created by an administrative error, the student must report it through the examination or academic office within the announced correction period.
or academic office within the announced correction period.

Progression from one semester to the next depends on the programme's academic requirements and any applicable backlog provisions. Students are expected to complete required credits in accordance with their programme structure.

A failed course remains part of the student's academic record until it is successfully cleared according to the applicable examination procedure. Passing a later course does not automatically erase a failed course unless the academic regulations explicitly provide for suc
s not automatically erase a failed course unless the academic regulations explicitly provide for such treatment.

The university maintains an academic record containing courses, grades, credits, examination outcomes, and other approved academic information. Students should report apparent errors through the designated academic-record correction process.

Requests for correction should identify the course, semester, nature of the suspected error, and supporting evidence. The submission of a correction request does not itself change the official record. A correction takes effect only after it has been approve
does not itself change the official record. A correction takes effect only after it has been approved and recorded by the competent office.

Students are expected to submit their own academic work except where collaboration is expressly permitted. Plagiarism, fabrication of data, impersonation, unauthorised collaboration, and unauthorised assistance during assessments may be treated as academic misconduct.

The presence of another student's work in a submission does not automatically establish who copied from whom. An academic authority may review the available evidence and apply the relevant disciplinary process.
y may review the available evidence and apply the relevant disciplinary process.

Where a programme contains project work, the project may include a proposal, progress review, final report, presentation, demonstration, or viva. The department may publish milestones for these components.

A student who misses a project milestone should contact the project supervisor or designated coordinator. Whether a missed milestone can be rescheduled depends on the rules applicable to that component and the reason for the absence.
omponent and the reason for the absence.

The student portal is the primary location for academic notices when a notice specifically identifies the portal as the communication channel. Email or another official channel may also be used where stated.

Students should retain copies of important submissions, receipts, approvals, and communications. A screenshot of a personal conversation with another student is not by itself an official academic approval.
emic approval.

When a rule requires approval from a department, examination office, academic committee, or other authority, the request must be submitted through the process prescribed for that authority. Approval by an unauthorised individual does not automatically satisfy a rule requiring approval from a specified authority.

Where two provisions appear to apply to the same situation, both provisions should be considered by the relevant decision-maker before determining the applicable rule.
considered by the relevant decision-maker before determining the applicable rule.

Students may submit requests for consideration in circumstances that are not directly addressed by a standard procedure. An exceptional-circumstances request does not guarantee approval. The competent authority may consider supporting evidence, timing, academic impact, and the relevant regulation.

A general statement that a situation is "urgent" does not itself establish eligibility for an exception.
ion.

These project regulations are intended to be read section by section. Definitions should be interpreted according to the document in which they appear unless a definition is expressly stated to apply across the entire corpus.

Where these regulations do not address a particular situation, no determination should be made from these provisions alone.

Attendance is recorded for scheduled teaching activities in accordance with the attendance procedure adopted by the relevant department. Students are responsible for being present at the scheduled start of the class or activity and for following the attendance-marking procedure.

Attendance should reflect actual participation. A student should not ask another student to mark attendance on the student's behalf. Any dispute concerning an attendance entry should be raised through the department's p
ent's behalf. Any dispute concerning an attendance entry should be raised through the department's prescribed process.

Attendance percentage is calculated from the sessions counted as attended and the sessions counted as scheduled for the relevant course or academic period. The calculation may differ between theory courses, practical courses, workshops, and other components where the programme rules prescribe a separate method.

Approved academic activities may be treated according to the relevant attendance procedure. Merely being physically present on campus does not automatically count as attendance in a part
dure. Merely being physically present on campus does not automatically count as attendance in a particular class.

Students must maintain at least **75% attendance in a course** to be eligible to appear for the corresponding end-semester examination, unless a specific approved exception applies.

A student below the required percentage should not assume that the shortfall will be automatically waived. Any condonation, exemption, or special consideration must be supported by the applicable procedure.

A student who expects to fall below the minimum should contact the appropriate academic authority as early as possible. The fact that a student attended most classes in a previous semester does not compensate for a shortage in the current course.

Attendance shortages are considered course by course unless a programme regulation expressly provides another method.

Medical absence is addressed separately in the Medical Leave Policy. A student who is ill should follow the medical-documentation and leave-submission procedure. Medical documentation by itself does not necessarily convert every missed class into attended sessions.

Where the Medical Leave Policy establishes a different examination-eligibility threshold for an approved medical case, that provision is relevant to the question and must be retrieved alongside the general 75% rule.
is relevant to the question and must be retrieved alongside the general 75% rule.

A student representing the institution in an officially authorised activity may request treatment of the absence under the applicable academic procedure. Approval is not automatic merely because an activity is described as university-related.

The request should normally identify the activity, dates, course affected, and approving authority. The department may require documentary evidence.

Students should report a suspected attendance-recording error within the period announced by the department. A complaint submitted after the record has been finalised may require additional verification.

A correction to an erroneous attendance record and an exemption from the minimum attendance requirement are different administrative matters and should be handled under their applicable provisions.
s.

Where internal assessment includes an attendance-related component, the calculation should follow the course or programme scheme. A student should not infer that satisfying the minimum examination attendance automatically produces full marks for an attendance component.

Periodic attendance reports may be made available through the student portal or department. Students should review reports before the correction period closes.

A student who sees 74% in an attendance report should not be told that the requirement is met merely because the student believes one missed class should not count. The relevant correction or exemption process must be followed.

The 75% attendance requirement is the general examination-eligibility requirement. Where another applicable provision establishes a specific exception for a particular circumstance, that provision should also be considered.

The applicable attendance requirement depends on the student's circumstances and the provisions governing those circumstances.

If a student has 82% attendance in Course A and 73% in Course B, the student satisfies the stated general minimum in Course A but does not satisfy it in Course B. The percentage for one course should not be averaged with another course to create eligibility for the second course.

Repeated late arrival may be addressed through course or departmental instructions. This document does not state that every late arrival must be converted into a fixed attendance deduction. Where no numerical penalty is specified, the applicable procedure should be consulted rather than assuming a fixed deduction.

A waiver request should identify the provision under which the student seeks consideration. Submission of a request does not itself grant a waiver.

Where a separate policy gives a committee authority to waive an attendance condition, the request should be considered under that authority and approval should not be assumed.

Students who are eligible for an end-semester examination must complete examination registration within the published period. Examination registration and semester registration are related but distinct administrative processes.

A student should verify the examination form before the deadline. A submitted form may not be editable after the correction window closes unless the examination office permits a correction.
mits a correction.

Eligibility to appear for an examination may depend on academic registration, attendance, outstanding requirements, and other programme-specific conditions. The general attendance requirement is stated in the Attendance Policy.

Where another policy establishes an exception for a particular circumstance, the exception must be considered together with the general requirement.

The examination timetable is published through the designated official channel. Students are expected to check the timetable and report apparent clashes through the prescribed correction process.

A student should not assume that two examinations scheduled on the same day are automatically a timetable conflict. The start and end times are relevant.

A student who does not appear for an examination receives the outcome prescribed by the applicable examination rules unless an approved absence procedure applies.

The ordinary examination policy does not provide a special entitlement to miss an examination for a family wedding, holiday, personal travel, or similar social event. Where a particular reason for absence is not addressed by the applicable examination provisions, no special exemption can be inferred from these rules alone.
ble examination provisions, no special exemption can be inferred from these rules alone.

A student unable to attend an examination because of illness should follow the medical-leave procedure and provide the required evidence within the stated period.

Approval of medical leave and permission to take a missed examination are separate questions unless a provision explicitly connects them.

Students must follow examination-room instructions, carry permitted materials, and comply with identity-verification procedures. Unauthorised materials or communication devices may be dealt with under the academic-integrity process.

A supplementary or repeat examination may be available for specified academic outcomes. Eligibility, timing, and fee requirements depend on the applicable examination notice or programme rule.

This document does not establish that every student who misses an examination automatically receives a supplementary examination.

A student may request the examination-result service identified in the relevant notice. Revaluation, verification, scrutiny, or another result-review process may have different eligibility conditions and deadlines.

A request should not be described as a guaranteed change in marks.

Where an examination fee applies, the amount and payment deadline should be taken from the relevant fee notice or fee schedule. If two applicable documents contain different deadlines for the same administrative action, both dates and their associated conditions should be considered.

Practical examinations, project evaluations, and viva voce assessments may have attendance, submission, or completion requirements in addition to written examination requirements.

A student should not infer that a rule about written examinations automatically governs a practical evaluation unless the corpus says so.
Students may be required to carry an institutional identity card or other documents for examination entry. Specific requirements should be checked against the applicable examination notice.

Questions about examination eligibility, timetable issues, missing marks, or procedural irregularities should be submitted to the designated office. A student should retain acknowledgement of the submission.

When considering examination eligibility, the provisions that directly address the student's circumstances should be considered together with any other applicable requirements.

Where the available provisions do not establish an answer, the applicable academic or administrative authority should be consulted.

This policy defines procedures for ordinary leave, medical absence, supporting documents, and requests for academic consideration. It includes a specific provision concerning examination eligibility in approved medical-leave cases.

Students may submit leave requests for circumstances recognised by the applicable academic procedure. A leave request should identify the dates, course or activity affected, reason, and supporting information where required.

Approval of ordinary leave does not automatically establish eligibility to miss an examination unless the relevant examination rules expressly provide for it.

A student who is medically unable to attend scheduled academic activities should submit the prescribed medical documentation through the designated process. The documentation should identify the relevant period and be sufficient for the competent authority to assess the request.

A medical certificate does not by itself guarantee approval. The competent authority may request additional information where the document is incomplete or unclear.
where the document is incomplete or unclear.

An approved medical-leave case may be considered for examination eligibility when course attendance is at least **60%**.

The provision applies where the medical leave has been properly approved and the conditions for medical consideration have been satisfied.

Medical documentation should be submitted within the period stated in the relevant notice or procedure. Late submission may require additional review.

The corpus does not state that every late medical submission must be rejected. Where no specific consequence is stated, the applicable procedure should be consulted.

Approval of medical leave concerns the student's absence. Permission to take a missed examination concerns examination eligibility or a separate examination procedure. These concepts should not be conflated.

Questions concerning a missed examination after medical leave should also be considered under the applicable examination provisions.

This policy does not establish a general examination exemption for family weddings, vacations, festivals, birthdays, or other social events. Questions about such circumstances depend on whether an applicable provision specifically addresses the reason for the absence.

Students facing a prolonged medical circumstance may submit a request for academic consideration. The request should describe the affected period and academic consequences. Approval remains subject to the competent authority.
Submitting altered or fabricated medical documentation may constitute misconduct and may be handled under the applicable disciplinary or academic-integrity procedure.
Students should retain copies of medical submissions, acknowledgements, and approvals. The absence of a personal copy does not itself prove that a submission was or was not received.

A medical approval can have different consequences depending on the provision invoked. A correction to an attendance record addresses whether a recorded absence was entered incorrectly. An exemption addresses whether a stated eligibility condition can be treated differently.

An exemption should not be treated as an attendance-record correction unless the applicable provision expressly makes that connection.
connection.

The medical attendance provision should be considered together with the general attendance requirement applicable to examination eligibility. The student's attendance percentage, approval status, and the circumstances covered by the medical provision are relevant when determining the applicable requirement.

> **Corpus status:** Synthetic project material created for controlled RuleGuard testing. This document is not an official Medi-Caps University publication and does not amend the authentic placement-policy PDF included in the corpus.

The corpus contains an authentic Medi-Caps University placement-policy PDF. This addendum is synthetic material created only for evaluating retrieval, citation, and conflict detection. It must never be presented as an official amendment to the authentic document.
section: 1. Relationship to the Authentic Placement Policy

text: Students participating in campus recruitment are expected to follow the procedures and penalties contained in the authentic placement-policy document. The authentic document states, among other provisions, that absence after registering for a recruitment process attracts a 20-point deduction and withdrawal after registration attracts a 30-point deduction.
A student who receives an offer through the placement process should follow the commitment and joining provisions stated in the authentic placement-policy document.
**Section PA-4.1:** For this synthetic corpus, a student who has accepted a campus placement offer shall not participate in any subsequent campus recruitment process.

A student who has accepted an offer may have an agreed joining date. The synthetic rule in this document does not by itself change the authentic placement policy's provisions concerning acceptance, joining, or placement discipline.

**Section PA-6.2:** For this synthetic corpus, a student who has accepted an offer may participate in a subsequent campus recruitment process until the date on which the student formally joins the organisation, provided the student satisfies the eligibility conditions for that recruitment process.

**This provision intentionally conflicts with Section PA-4.1.**

The conflict is deliberate. A question such as "I accepted an offer but have not joined the company yet; can I sit for another campus drive?" should retrieve both PA-4.1 and PA-6.2.

The correct classification is CONFLICT because the two provisions give incompatible answers to the same circumstance.
The authentic placement policy contains a penalty framework. This synthetic addendum should not be used to invent a new numerical penalty unless a section expressly states one.

Students should follow mandatory placement-readiness activities and other instructions in the authentic placement policy. Questions about penalties should cite the authentic PDF when that is the source of the rule.
The authentic policy addresses independent off-campus placement participation and requires prior permission. This addendum does not override that provision.

The RuleGuard interface should distinguish between evidence from the authentic PDF and evidence from this synthetic addendum. The source name and section reference should make that distinction visible.

This conflict is a controlled evaluation case. It demonstrates why a system that retrieves only one high-similarity passage can produce a misleading answer. The intended system should retrieve multiple relevant passages and detect incompatible conditions.

This policy defines a scholarship framework covering eligibility, renewal, documentation, review, suspension, and administrative handling. It describes common requirements for scholarship applications and renewal.

A scholarship applicant must satisfy the eligibility conditions stated for the relevant scholarship category. Conditions may include academic performance, enrolment status, financial documentation, attendance, or another requirement expressly stated in the scholarship notice.

A student should not assume that satisfying one condition guarantees the scholarship. Eligibility is determined using all applicable conditions.
applicable conditions.

Scholarship applications should be submitted through the designated process before the stated deadline. An incomplete application may be returned for correction if the procedure permits correction.

The student is responsible for ensuring that uploaded documents are legible and correspond to the requested information. A successful upload does not necessarily mean that the application has been approved.
oved.

Supporting documents may include academic records, identity documents, income-related documents, bank information, or other documents identified in the scholarship notice.

The policy does not establish a universal list of documents for every scholarship. Where a required document is not specified for the relevant scholarship, the applicable scholarship notice should be consulted.

A renewal applicant must satisfy the renewal conditions applicable to the scholarship. Renewal is not automatic merely because the student received a scholarship in the previous academic period.

The fee schedule lists a standard scholarship-renewal deadline of 15 August and a late-action date of 22 August. A separate scholarship memorandum states that renewal applications submitted by 20 August will be accepted without late classification. The applicable notice or memorandum should be considere
ill be accepted without late classification. The applicable notice or memorandum should be considered when determining the relevant deadline.

Where a scholarship notice specifies an academic-performance threshold, the student's academic record should be evaluated using the method stated in that notice. This corpus does not establish one universal percentage or CGPA threshold for every scholarship.

A student should not be told that a particular CGPA guarantees renewal unless the relevant rule explicitly says so.

Some scholarships may contain an attendance condition, but this document does not create a universal scholarship attendance threshold. Questions about attendance eligibility should be answered from the applicable attendance or scholarship provision.

Where financial need is part of a scholarship category, the applicant may be required to provide evidence specified by the relevant notice. A student's statement that financial circumstances have changed is not, by itself, a defined numerical eligibility criterion in this corpus.

The scholarship authority may verify submitted information. If a discrepancy is identified, the applicant may be asked to provide clarification or additional documentation.

The submission of a document for verification does not automatically establish that the document has been accepted as valid.

This corpus does not establish a universal rule allowing or prohibiting every combination of scholarships. A question about combining two named scholarships should be answered only if a provision addresses that combination.

Approved scholarship amounts may be disbursed according to the administrative schedule applicable to the scholarship. Approval and disbursement are separate events.

A student should not interpret an application acknowledgement as proof that payment has been released.

Where bank information is required, the student should provide the information in the format prescribed by the scholarship process. Errors may delay processing.

The corpus does not specify a particular bank, branch, or payment application as universally mandatory.

A scholarship may be suspended where the applicable scholarship rules provide for suspension. A suspension decision should identify the reason and applicable procedure.

The corpus does not state that every disciplinary action automatically cancels every scholarship.
A student who withdraws from a programme may have scholarship consequences under the applicable scholarship conditions. This document does not establish a universal refund or repayment formula.
A change of programme may affect scholarship eligibility where the scholarship category is tied to a specific programme. Students should seek a determination through the designated process.

Where a scholarship is awarded on the basis of financial need, a material change may need to be reported if the applicable notice requires it. The corpus does not define a universal monetary threshold for what counts as material.

A standard deadline and a late-action deadline are different concepts. The existence of a late-action date does not necessarily mean that the application will receive the same treatment as an on-time application.

The separate 15 August and 20 August provisions provide different dates and conditions for scholarship renewal. Both should be considered when determining the applicable deadline.
A late application may require additional approval, documentation, or review when the relevant notice says so. The corpus does not state that every late application must be rejected.

Where a scholarship decision is subject to an appeal process, the applicant should follow the deadline and submission method stated in the relevant notice. This corpus does not provide a universal appeal period.

If an applicant discovers an error before the correction period closes, the applicant should use the prescribed correction mechanism. Sending a second application does not automatically cancel the first application unless the procedure says so.
This policy does not establish a universal penalty for submitting duplicate applications. Any consequence depends on the applicable procedure.
Submitting false or fabricated information may lead to review under the applicable academic or administrative procedure. The exact consequence depends on the relevant rule and circumstances.
Students should monitor official notices, maintain copies of submissions, and verify application status. Failure to read a published notice does not automatically extend a deadline.
A student may ask the designated office for clarification about an application. Informal advice should not be treated as a formal approval where the policy requires a documented decision.
Where a scholarship category requires committee review, the committee may consider the evidence and applicable criteria. A request for committee review does not guarantee a positive outcome.
Scholarship applications may contain sensitive financial and academic information. The corpus does not create a general right for one student to inspect another student's application.
The scholarship authority may retain records required for administration and verification. Students should retain their own acknowledgement or receipt where available.

If a scholarship category is not described in this policy, its eligibility and administrative requirements cannot be determined from this document alone. Rules applicable to another scholarship category should not automatically be applied.

For scholarship renewal, the fee schedule lists 15 August as a standard deadline. A separate memorandum provides another date for acceptance of renewal applications without late classification.

For a scholarship category not described in this policy, the applicable eligibility and renewal requirements should be obtained from the relevant scholarship notice.

The scholarship provisions cover several related administrative concepts, including renewal, approval, deadlines, eligibility, and documentation.

Where multiple provisions concern the same administrative action, they should be considered together. Where the available information is incomplete, the applicable scholarship notice or administrative record should be consulted.

An application can have statuses such as submitted, under review, approved, returned for correction, rejected, or otherwise recorded according to the process. The exact status should be taken from the record rather than inferred from the student's expectation. A student who has submitted documents should not be told that the scholarship is approved unless the corpus contains an approval provision or status confirming it.

A standard deadline and a late-action date are different concepts. Where multiple dates appear in applicable administrative documents, the dates and their stated conditions should be considered together.

This synthetic policy does not establish rules for employment contracts, taxation, immigration, transportation, food services, personal banking, or other topics outside university scholarship administration. Questions concerning those subjects should be addressed under the applicable university regulation or administrative procedure.

Each scholarship provision should be interpreted together with its stated section, date, condition, and source document. Where a table or memorandum supplies a date, the relevant row or provision should be considered together with the surrounding administrative context.

Students are expected to follow reasonable instructions issued through authorised university channels and to conduct themselves respectfully in academic and residential environments.

Students may be required to carry an institutional identity card for specified academic, examination, laboratory, hostel, or placement activities. The exact requirement should be taken from the rule applicable to that activity.
Misconduct may include behaviour expressly prohibited by an applicable policy. The consequences depend on the relevant rule and disciplinary procedure.

A student who wishes to report an administrative or academic issue should use the designated grievance or departmental process. A complaint should state the relevant facts and attach available evidence.

Documents, official acknowledgements, portal records, and other authorised records may be considered in administrative review. Informal statements from other students should not automatically be treated as official decisions.

Where a rule assigns authority to a committee, the committee's decision should be recorded through the applicable procedure. A student should not assume that an individual staff member can exercise a power assigned specifically to a committee.
A student may submit a request for exceptional consideration when the ordinary regulations do not adequately address a documented circumstance. Submission does not guarantee approval.

Official decisions should be communicated through an authorised channel. A message saying "it should be okay" is not equivalent to a formal approval when the applicable regulation requires documented approval.

Students should provide accurate information in academic and administrative submissions. Corrections should be made through the prescribed procedure rather than by altering an already-issued document.
Where an appeal mechanism exists, the student should submit the appeal within the applicable period and identify the decision being challenged.

Students should avoid sharing another person's academic record or personal information unnecessarily. This corpus does not create a general entitlement to access another student's confidential record.
Where this policy does not address a particular situation, the applicable university regulation or administrative procedure should be consulted rather than assuming that a general practice applies.

Administrative decisions should be based on the applicable provisions and supporting records. Where a matter is governed by a specific procedure, that procedure should be consulted together with any relevant supporting documentation.
